article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Balanced Hybrid
Genetics: Magic Bullet × Strawberries & Cream
Breeder: Exotic Genetix
THC Content: 7–12%
CBD Content: 12–15%
Terpene Profile: Myrcene , beta-caryophyllene , limonene
Primary Flavors: Blueberry, sweet berries, creamy vanilla
Flowering Time (Indoor): 50–60 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: Late September through October
Indoor Yield: Heavy
Outdoor Yield: High
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Imagine opening a container of cannabis and encountering the fragrance of blueberry pastries before the familiar herbal character of marijuana becomes apparent. That unusual sensory contrast captures much of what makes Mystic Magic interesting. Created by Exotic Genetix, this hybrid combines the CBD-oriented genetics of Magic Bullet with the dessert-inspired characteristics of Strawberries & Cream. The result is a distinctive breeding project that connects cannabinoid diversity with the aromatic complexity associated with contemporary American cannabis.

While many modern weed varieties emphasize increasingly high THC percentages, this cultivar draws attention to a different possibility: combining meaningful CBD potential with moderate psychoactive effects and an appealing flavor profile. Certain expressions offer an uplifting, mentally engaging experience without the intensity associated with high-potency marijuana. Others may contain substantially more THC, making individual laboratory results especially important. Beyond its cannabinoid potential, the plant offers a relatively short flowering cycle, vigorous branching, and the capacity for substantial flower production.
Genetics and Lineage

Mystic Magic originated from Exotic Genetix’s crossing of Magic Bullet with Strawberries & Cream. The breeder identifies Magic Bullet as the maternal parent and Strawberries & Cream as the paternal parent. Its original genetic classification is a balanced 50/50 hybrid, although some descriptions characterize individual expressions as slightly sativa-leaning. This distinction matters because indica and sativa percentages are broad breeding classifications rather than precise measurements of effects or chemical composition. The cultivar’s more important genetic characteristic is the combination of a CBD-focused parent with a flavorful THC-producing hybrid.

Magic Bullet introduces an unusual element to the family tree. Its documented ancestry traces to The Wife and Otto II, two cannabis lines associated with CBD-rich breeding. The Wife belongs to a group of cultivars selected for substantial cannabidiol production, while Otto genetics have played a role in developing plants with relatively low intoxicating potential and elevated CBD concentrations. Descriptions of Magic Bullet include examples with very high CBD and minimal delta-9 THC, although those figures cannot be transferred directly to its offspring. When crossed with a THC-producing parent, cannabinoid inheritance can produce considerable variation among seedlings, including different THC-to-CBD ratios.

Strawberries & Cream supplies the dessert-oriented side of the combination. Exotic Genetix’s lineage connects this parent to Strawberry Jelly and Cookies & Cream , bringing together fruit-heavy aromatics and the resinous qualities associated with the Cookies genetic family . Strawberry Jelly has connections to Mimosa genetics, which descend from Clementine and Purple Punch , while Cookies & Cream combines Girl Scout Cookies with Starfighter genetics. These ancestral influences help explain the potential for sweet berries, citrus accents, creamy undertones, and abundant trichome development. Through this pairing, the breeder created a hybrid that offers opportunities for both flavorful flower selection and cannabinoid-focused phenotype hunting.
Effects and Experience

Mystic Magic is commonly associated with an uplifting experience that emphasizes mental engagement rather than immediate physical heaviness. The initial effects may include improved mood, greater interest in conversation, and a pleasant sense of motivation. Creative activities, music, and relaxed social interactions can feel more engaging, particularly when the flower has a moderate THC concentration. Some consumers describe a clearer and more functional experience than they encounter with stronger marijuana varieties, although this response depends on dosage and the actual cannabinoid composition.

A notable distinction involves the potential presence of substantial CBD. Cannabidiol interacts with several physiological signaling systems and has effects that differ from those of THC. In some circumstances, CBD may influence how THC is experienced, but it does not consistently prevent intoxication or eliminate anxiety. A flower containing both cannabinoids can therefore feel quite different from a THC-dominant product, even when the two are otherwise similar in appearance or aroma. Higher-CBD selections may produce relatively gentle psychoactive effects, whereas THC-heavy phenotypes can generate stronger euphoria, altered perception, and impaired attention.

As the experience develops, the initial mental stimulation may settle into a comfortable physical calm. Rather than producing unavoidable couch-lock, moderate exposures may leave some individuals relaxed while remaining conversational. Nevertheless, the cultivar should not automatically be considered non-intoxicating. Dry mouth, dizziness, temporary changes in concentration, and anxiety remain possible, especially with higher-THC batches. Consumers should begin with a small amount, evaluate the response gradually, and avoid driving or performing safety-sensitive activities after using cannabis.
Medical Benefits

The cannabinoid heritage of Mystic Magic makes it particularly interesting from a medical cannabis perspective. Some descriptions of the strain identify CBD concentrations around 12–15% alongside moderate THC levels, although those numbers represent particular reported expressions rather than guaranteed characteristics. CBD and THC have different pharmacological actions, creating interest in preparations that contain both compounds. Research involving cannabis-based medicines suggests that certain cannabinoid combinations may provide modest benefits for selected chronic pain conditions. However, no controlled clinical trials establish this specific cultivar as an effective treatment for chronic pain, inflammation, or other medical disorders.

Stress-related symptoms are another reason some consumers seek balanced cannabinoid products. A CBD-rich phenotype may appeal to individuals who wish to avoid the intense psychoactive sensations associated with high-THC weed. The cultivar’s reported combination of mental uplift and physical calm could also be attractive to people seeking relaxation without pronounced sedation. Still, evidence supporting cannabis as a treatment for anxiety disorders , depression, PTSD , or ADHD remains limited or inconsistent. THC can aggravate anxiety in susceptible individuals, and the presence of CBD should not be regarded as a guarantee against unwanted psychological effects.

Questions about inflammation, sleep, and nausea also arise when discussing CBD-containing marijuana. Although cannabinoids are being investigated for these applications, findings from laboratory studies or specific pharmaceutical preparations cannot be assumed to apply to Mystic Magic flower. Individuals considering medical use should review the tested THC and CBD concentrations, discuss possible medication interactions with a qualified clinician, and avoid replacing established treatments without medical guidance. Smoking cannabis also exposes the respiratory system to harmful combustion products, making inhalation an important consideration for people with asthma or other lung conditions.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The defining sensory impression of Mystic Magic is its pastry-like berry sweetness. Blueberry occupies a prominent position in many flavor descriptions, accompanied by sugary fruit, soft cream, and a delicate nuttiness. Unlike sharper citrus hybrids that emphasize sourness or fuel, this cultivar may present a rounded aroma reminiscent of blueberry pie filling and lightly toasted dessert crust. Breaking apart well-cured flowers can reveal an additional layer of earthy herbs and subtle pepper, adding complexity beneath the sweeter surface.

The flavor may begin with ripe berries and a creamy sweetness before transitioning toward a mild nutty or spicy finish. Certain phenotypes can also express faint citrus or tropical-fruit accents inherited through the Strawberries & Cream family. These distinctions depend on genetics, cultivation conditions, and postharvest handling. Excessively rapid drying can strip away delicate fruit aromatics, while properly cured flower is more likely to preserve the contrast between sweet and earthy notes.

Myrcene is frequently identified as a prominent terpene associated with Mystic Magic. Its herbal, earthy character can complement the cultivar’s sweet fruit aromas. Beta-caryophyllene, which appears in the Magic Bullet parent profile, may contribute peppery depth, while limonene is a plausible contributor to citrus characteristics in certain selections. However, an aromatic description cannot establish a definitive terpene ranking. The actual composition of each batch should be determined through laboratory analysis rather than assumed from its name or genetic ancestry.
Growing Information

Mystic Magic is a photoperiod cannabis hybrid developed for cultivation in suitable indoor and outdoor environments. Exotic Genetix describes the plant as a medium-to-tall, multi-topped bush capable of heavy production. This growth pattern suggests substantial lateral branching, with multiple flowering sites developing across the canopy. Rather than relying exclusively on one large central flower, mature plants can distribute production among numerous branches. Because the original release consists of regular seeds, growers must distinguish male and female plants when their objective is seedless flower production. Selecting and preserving a desirable female phenotype can be particularly valuable when cannabinoid ratios are a priority.

Indoors, the breeder’s flowering estimate of 50–60 days makes this cultivar a relatively quick-finishing photoperiod hybrid. Individual plants may require more time depending on phenotype and conditions. Adequate light distribution helps support lower flowering sites, while sensible canopy management prevents excessive crowding. The plant’s potential for dense, resin-coated flowers also makes humidity control and air movement important as maturity approaches. Blue-green coloration, orange pistils, and occasional darker foliage may appear in some expressions, but pigmentation varies and cannot be used as a reliable indicator of cannabinoid potency.

Outdoor cultivation benefits from consistent sunlight, healthy root development, and protection against prolonged rainfall during flowering. In the Northern Hemisphere, harvest may occur from late September into October, depending on seasonal conditions and latitude. The breeder describes Mystic Magic as a heavy producer, although standardized yield figures in grams per square meter or grams per outdoor plant are not available. Yield also does not establish cannabinoid quality: two visually similar plants may contain very different proportions of THC and CBD. Growers interested in preserving the strain’s CBD potential should prioritize laboratory testing of selected phenotypes, alongside evaluation of aroma, growth structure, and flower quality.
FAQ
Is Mystic Magic an indica or sativa strain?

Mystic Magic is a balanced hybrid originally classified by Exotic Genetix as 50% indica and 50% sativa. Some descriptions characterize it as slightly sativa-dominant because of its reported uplifting and mentally engaging effects. However, the traditional indica-sativa distinction cannot reliably predict how a particular batch will affect an individual. Cannabinoid concentrations, terpene composition, dose, and personal sensitivity are more informative.
Is Mystic Magic high in CBD?

Mystic Magic has the genetic potential to produce CBD-rich flowers because Magic Bullet, one of its parents, comes from CBD-focused breeding lines. Some published strain descriptions list approximately 12–15% CBD. Other commercial examples may contain substantially different cannabinoid ratios, including higher THC levels. A verified laboratory report is necessary to determine whether an individual batch is genuinely CBD-rich.
How much THC does Mystic Magic contain?

CBD-rich versions are commonly described as containing approximately 7–12% THC, while other listings place particular selections closer to 18%. This variation is important because regular-seed offspring can inherit different cannabinoid characteristics. Consumers should not assume that a product is mildly intoxicating solely because of the strain name or its CBD ancestry.
What does Mystic Magic taste like?

The strain is associated with sweet blueberry, mixed berries, creamy pastry, and delicate nutty flavors. Some phenotypes introduce mild citrus, tropical fruit, earthy herbs, or peppery spice. Its aromatic character is generally more dessert-oriented than heavily diesel-dominant cannabis varieties. Proper curing and storage help preserve the volatile compounds responsible for these distinctive impressions.
How long does Mystic Magic take to flower, and is it easy to grow?

The original breeder describes a flowering period of approximately 50–60 days, with heavy yield potential and a medium-to-tall bush structure. Its growth characteristics can make it productive in a managed environment, but regular seeds and cannabinoid variability introduce additional considerations. Moderate cultivation experience is useful, especially for growers hoping to identify and preserve CBD-rich phenotypes.
Final Thoughts on Mystic Magic

Mystic Magic occupies an interesting position in the cannabis landscape because its breeding combines two objectives that are not always pursued together: CBD-oriented cannabinoid development and premium dessert-style flower characteristics. Exotic Genetix brought Magic Bullet together with Strawberries & Cream to create a hybrid with the potential for substantial CBD content, appealing berry aromas, and a comparatively balanced experience.

The cultivar also offers meaningful horticultural advantages. Its short flowering period, branching structure, and heavy-production potential make it attractive to growers interested in efficient cultivation. At the same time, the genetic variation possible in regular seeds creates opportunities to identify individual plants with distinctive cannabinoid profiles, aromatic characteristics, and flower development.

For consumers, the most important consideration is recognizing that Mystic Magic does not have one universally consistent THC-to-CBD ratio. A CBD-rich selection may provide a noticeably different experience from a high-THC phenotype carrying the same name. When evaluated through accurate laboratory testing, this flavorful hybrid offers an example of how modern cannabis breeding can explore cannabinoid diversity while retaining the sensory qualities that make specialty marijuana cultivars appealing.
